analysis.title: Global Fund Manager Survey: A light hits the boom on the grey
key_insights: November FMS (survey period Nov 6-12, 169 respondents to global questions, $461bn AUM) shows investors bullish on macro and markets but ending the boom and AI euphoria. BofA stays tactically risk-off because the survey shows too little investor fear to buy risk.

Only 3% of investors predict a hard landing. Cash fell to 3.6% from 3.9%, the lowest since Aug'26. A drop in cash with no large pullback in bull sentiment suggests there is not yet enough fear to buy.

The base case is now soft landing at 50% of investors, overtaking no landing at 42%, for the first time since June. Boom expectations (above-trend growth and inflation) fell to 41% from 47% in October, which was the highest since Feb'22.

Net 14% of investors expect global growth to decelerate over the next 12 months (net 4% last month), the most since Apr'26. Net 32% expect lower global CPI in 12 months (net 5% last month), the lowest inflation expectations since Oct'24.

Investors cut tech overweight to net 12% from net 37%, the biggest monthly cut since Jun'06. BofA notes that FMS history suggests the best entry points for tech come when investors cut it to underweight.

AI capex is the main micro message. A record net 38% say companies are overinvesting, only 16% want companies to raise capex (lowest since May'20), and 52% expect an AI hyperscaler to announce a capex cut in the next 6 months, up from 30% last month.

The top tail risks are both AI-related: AI bubble at 34% and AI hyperscaler credit event at 31%. Inflation and a disorderly rise in bond yields, the top tail risk in October, have receded. Geopolitical peace is cited by 5%.
38% of investors name AI hyperscaler bonds as the most likely source of a systemic credit event, followed by private credit at 30%, government debt at 15%, leveraged ETFs at 8% and crypto at 1%.
Long global semiconductors remains the most crowded trade at 39%, down from a 82% peak in July. Short China stocks is second at 14% and long Magnificent 7 third at 12%.
BofA identifies the consensus bear risk as global rate hikes leading to recession, and the consensus bull risk as concerns over a tech credit event reversing.

Investors cut their bond underweight by 13ppt, the biggest monthly increase in allocation since Apr'25, to net 23% underweight, the least since Nov'25. A 10-year UST yield of 5.8% (weighted average) would prompt a shift from stocks to bonds, with 34% saying 6.0% and 30% saying 5.5%.
A record net 23% of investors say gold is undervalued. Gold is expected to end 2027 at $4,341/oz against a current $3,868.

Sector moves: allocation to healthcare rose to net 34% overweight from 23%. Consumer discretionary and staples saw the biggest combined monthly jump in allocation since Jun'06 (discretionary net 20% underweight from 34%, staples net 18% underweight from 32%). Energy fell to net 12% underweight from net 4% overweight, and materials to net 9% underweight, the most since Nov'25.

Allocation moves: investors increased consumer discretionary, staples, bonds and healthcare and reduced tech, US dollar, cash and Japan. Equity allocation is net 41% overweight (from 44%), cash net 9% underweight, commodities net 15% overweight (from 21%), and real estate net 23% underweight.

Regional allocation: net 13% overweight US equities (from 11%), net 28% overweight EM (from 34%), net neutral Japan (from net 9% overweight), net 5% underweight Eurozone (from 8%) and net 21% underweight UK (from 26%).

2027 views: international equities are expected to be the best asset class (36%) ahead of US equities (24%) and gold (17%). Nasdaq and MSCI EM tie as the best equity index at 21% each, with Euro Stoxx at 19%. The Japanese yen is the expected best currency at 42%, ahead of the US dollar at 16%.
YE-2027 investor targets: 10-year UST yield 4.9% (current 5.1%), EURUSD 1.12 (current 1.10), S&P 500 7,926 (current 7,562), gold $4,341/oz (current $3,868).

BofA contrarian trades based on extreme November FMS positions: long cash/gold versus short stocks, long consumer versus short health care, long REITs versus short banks, and long energy versus short industrials.

BofA Global FMS Cash Rule currently reads 3.6% with a Sell signal. The Bull & Bear Indicator is unchanged at 7.4 (Neutral). The broader sentiment measure dipped to 6.3 from 6.4, the least bullish since Jun'26.

Investors expect quality and large caps to lead over the next 12 months: net 71% say high-quality earnings beat low-quality, net 38% large caps beat small caps, net 36% high dividend yield beats low, and net 35% low volatility beats high volatility. Investors are taking net 4% lower than normal risk, from net 9% lower in October.

risk_factors: Global rate hikes leading to recession is the consensus bear risk per the FMS.
AI bubble (34%) and AI hyperscaler credit event (31%) are the top two tail risks.
Hyperscaler bonds (38%) and private credit (30%) are seen as the most likely sources of a systemic credit event.
A hyperscaler capex cut, expected by 52% of investors within 6 months.
Crowded long positioning in global semiconductors (39% name it the most crowded trade).
Second wave of inflation (14%) and a disorderly rise in bond yields (13%) remain tail risks, though they have receded.
charts_described: Chart 1 plots the monthly change in net % overweight tech, with the November 2026 drop the largest since Jun'06.
Chart 3 shows soft landing expectations at 50% overtaking no landing at 42%, with 3% expecting a hard landing.
Chart 4 shows FMS average cash falling to 3.6% from 3.9%, lowest since Aug'26.
Chart 12 shows long global semiconductors as the most crowded trade at 39%, down from a Jul'26 peak of 82%.
Chart 15 shows a weighted average 10-year UST yield of 5.8% needed to shift allocation from stocks to bonds.
Chart 17 shows November monthly allocation changes, with rotation into consumer discretionary, staples, bonds and healthcare and out of tech, USD, cash and Japan.
Chart 51 shows net sector overweights, with pharma at 34% net overweight and discretionary at 20% net underweight.
vol_and_positioning: Most crowded trades: long global semiconductors 39% (down from a 82% peak in July), short China stocks 14%, long Magnificent 7 12%, short Treasuries 10%, long US dollar 8%, long oil 5%.
FMS cash at 3.6% triggers a Sell on BofA's Cash Rule, which sells at 4.0% or below and buys at 5.0% or above.
Bull & Bear Indicator at 7.4 is Neutral. BofA sells global equities above 8.0 and buys below 2.0.
Net 41% overweight global equities, 0.6 stdev above average. Net 9% underweight cash, 1.9 stdev below average. Net 23% underweight bonds, 0.7 stdev above average.
Net 40% of investors say the US dollar is overvalued (from 36%), 0.9 stdev above average. Net 10% say the euro is undervalued.
The FMS Financial Market Stability Risks Indicator rose to -0.6 from -0.9, with emerging market, credit, business cycle and counterparty risk components all increasing.

Hedging and trade idea from BofA: contrarian positions on FMS extremes are long cash/gold versus short stocks, long consumer versus short health care, long REITs versus short banks, and long energy versus short industrials.
geopolitical: Geopolitical peace is cited as a tail risk by 5% of respondents, versus 34% for AI bubble.
Short China stocks is the second most crowded trade at 14%.
